parallel.requirements: Implement a complete Pandarallel-compatible library with DataFrame, Series, groupby, rolling, expanding, progress bars, packaging, docs, and official pytest acceptance.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent implemented and integrated the code, then launched a workflow that split adversarial verification across dimension-specific child agents and verifier children.
parallel.implementation: The parent started from/reference-compared upstream Pandarallel, patched pandas 2.3 and empty-data behavior, added package files, docs, assets, and tests, and reached local 217-test success before the workflow audit.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered the workspace artifact with package modules, setup files, docs, tests, and generated assets; artifact validation and official evaluation accepted the tree.
parallel.verification: Parallel ran upstream/master tests and a workflow audit; official status later reports 217 passed out of 217, but the workflow audit did not return a final aggregate result.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official testcase remained failing, but the late verifier workflow had unreturned findings and one child had to discard contaminated /dev/shm observations.

serial.requirements: Implement the same Pandarallel task and acceptance surface in a single-agent run without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The serial agent kept pandas-internals research, implementation, test authoring, hardening, and final delivery under one parent trajectory.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote the Pandarallel modules directly, validated groupby and window behavior against pandas internals, and added broad local tests and extra edge-case tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial delivered a package workspace with modules and tests; artifact validation and official evaluation accepted the tree.
serial.verification: Serial ran 980 tests successfully, hardened extra cases to 194 passing tests, and then passed official evaluation with 217 of 217 tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official testcase remained failing; any remaining latent behavior differences did not affect the completed official result and there were no child results to consume.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the Pandarallel task: implement pandas parallel apply/map/groupby/rolling/expanding behavior, packaging, docs, tests, memory-fs and pipe transports, and official pytest acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run worked from the same prompt and recognized the same implementation and testing obligations for Pandarallel without child delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference reached the evaluator; both delivered artifacts passed the same 217 official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation and later delegated a broad read-only audit workflow across probe dimensions and verification children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial control kept implementation, probing, and hardening in one actor; status records show no workflow calls or child logs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added verifier-child ownership after a passing implementation, while serial stayed monolithic.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verifier briefs carried a detailed API and grading contract to children, including data operations, pandas comparison method, and read-only constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained the task context locally while editing the implementation and extra tests directly.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel context had to cross workflow child boundaries; serial context remained in a single trajectory.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied/reference-built Pandarallel, patched pandas 2.3 compatibility and empty-data behavior, then wrote package, docs, and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial authored the Pandarallel implementation directly, validated pandas internals, then hardened groupby and exception behavior with local tests.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced functional implementations, but parallel leaned on a later workflow audit while serial used direct local probe/test iterations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child verifier results entered the workflow journal, including concrete defect reports, but the workflow state never returned a final aggregate to the parent.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all local findings and fixes were immediately in the parent context.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unreturned verifier-result boundary; serial had no equivalent boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verifier children shared /dev/shm and one child observed sibling-created pandarallel files and processes as contamination before isolating with a private root.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial status shows no delegation or parallel child logs, so no sibling verifier processes shared scratch state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced cross-child temporary environment interference; serial did not have shared child state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran upstream/master tests with 217 passing before launching the workflow audit and later passed official evaluation 217/217.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran a larger direct local suite, including 980 passing tests and 194 extra passing tests, and passed official evaluation 217/217.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial kept verification local and completed; parallel obtained additional child findings that did not get folded back into a final parent decision, though official acceptance was still complete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used one workflow with 13 child logs and reached the 2399-second agent timeout, leaving the workflow aggregate incomplete while the artifact still passed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also reached the outer timeout, but without workflow calls, child logs, or unreturned child results.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent late budget on a concurrent audit and closed with unreturned workflow state; serial spent the budget on direct implementation and testing.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed status records show both modes passed the same Pandarallel evaluation, 217 of 217 tests. The concrete task-solving difference is process-level rather than outcome-level: parallel solved and tested the package, then launched a concurrent verifier workflow whose useful findings did not return to the parent and whose children shared /dev/shm; serial solved and tested directly without those child-boundary failures.
parallel_contributors: Passing implementation and local 217-test run before workflow launch; late workflow audit created adverse process evidence without changing official pass status.
serial_contributors: Direct single-agent implementation and local broad tests, with no child result lifecycle or shared child environment.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial and parallel used different internal hardening paths and local test breadth, but the official evaluator did not distinguish them.

candidates.reason: Parallel had an active implementation owner in the parent, which wrote the library source and tests before launching verifier children.
The parent owned integration of the source files; child agents were verifiers rather than separately owned implementation components requiring integration.
The parent assembled the required workspace package, setup files, docs, tests, and artifact tree before evaluation.
The parent controlled the implementation, local test, workflow audit launch, and delivery pipeline, even though the later verifier workflow did not return cleanly.
Parallel implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; the parent implemented and tested before the workflow audit.
The parallel workflow was launched after a passing implementation path, not as a completed investigation phase that deferred productive implementation until too late.
No indispensable implementation path was starved of workers; the main implementation and local tests completed before the verifier workflow problem.

The workflow was broad and the agent process timed out, but the direct retained boundary is that concrete verifier findings failed to return to the parent; high fan-out alone is not the retained pattern.
No single child had a uniquely overbroad assigned task that left indispensable implementation unfinished; the adverse chain involved workflow result return and shared environment evidence.
The verifier prompts included task context, files, comparison method, and read-only instructions; no known requirement was omitted from a child brief in a way that made its work unusable.
Children were independent probes/verifiers, not separately owned implementation components with missing interoperability contracts that produced incompatible code.
No known parent finding is shown disappearing through a summary or transfer; the retained handoff problem is that verifier results did not return to the parent at all.
The child findings were not available to the parent as an oversized completed handoff; the workflow aggregate remained absent.
No receiver acted on superseded workspace or requirement information; observed inconsistencies were either live /dev/shm contamination or unreturned verifier findings.
Verifier children sometimes disagreed, but there was no parent-visible conflicting handoff that remained unadjudicated and drove an integration decision.
The parent had local and official acceptance evidence, including 217/217 official tests; no unsupported whole-task completion decision with a visible unresolved integrated requirement is shown.
There was no replacement child retry that repeated prior work because it lacked inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: Several verifier children were interrupted when the run ended, but the retained episode is the concrete finding trapped below the workflow aggregate, not a separate stopped-child implementation dependency.
There was no complete unpromoted candidate or component set waiting for final placement; the workspace had already been delivered and passed official evaluation.
No child implementation was merged only after integrated verification; children were read-only or audit probes after the main implementation.
The workflow children did not produce delegated implementation code that needed to be joined into the final artifact.

The parallel parent launched a workflow of verifier agents after local implementation and tests. At least one verifier returned concrete defects into the workflow journal, but the workflow state ended with a null aggregate result, so those verifier findings were not returned to or consumed by the parent before closure.
candidates.realized_consequence: Concrete verifier findings remained below the workflow boundary and did not affect the delivered passing artifact or final closure decision.
candidates.near_match_reason: The findings are visible in child and workflow records, but the parent-facing workflow aggregate never completed; this is a missing return, not a completed result that the parent received and ignored.

candidates.reason: Cancelled or interrupted verifier children were part of the same terminal workflow-audit chain and did not leave a required implementation scope for parent takeover.
The nearest case to Missing Verifier Return is rejected because the parent did not receive a completed workflow result to inspect.
The parent was not merely idle without inspecting available parent-facing results; the important failure was absence of a returned workflow aggregate despite child findings.
No concurrent agents produced competing source implementations in different files that required reconciliation.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file and reconciling or observing each other's concurrent source changes.
No agent replaced another agent's non-entry source module.
No child replaced the submitted entry point or required deliverable while another actor owned it.
No broad cleanup or rebuild invalidated another agent's final-tree output or provenance.
Shared workspace writes were not the realized problem; the observed interference was shared /dev/shm temp files and processes during verifier execution.

Concurrent verifier children shared the same /dev/shm namespace. One child observed pandarallel temp files and Python processes from sibling probes, identified those observations as cross-contamination, and reran with a private MEMORY_FS_ROOT to get clean evidence.
candidates.realized_consequence: A verifier initially treated sibling-created temp files and processes as leak or FileNotFound evidence, then had to spend extra probe time isolating the memory filesystem to discard the contaminated observations.
candidates.near_match_reason: The concrete interference was in shared temporary files and processes under /dev/shm during verification, not multiple agents writing or overwriting the source workspace or final deliverable tree.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Rejected Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, Blind Timeout Wait, and Fan-out Budget Exhaustion as separate labels for the same unfinished workflow-audit chain.
Rejected Unisolated Workspace Writes and write-collision labels for the /dev/shm episode because the concrete interference was temporary environment contamination, not source or deliverable writes.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were reviewed; the only retained independent episodes with realized parallel-side adverse consequences were Missing Verifier Return and Artifact Leakage.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No numeric cap was imposed; downstream timeout, child interruption, no-takeover, and unused-result candidates were suppressed when they restated the retained verifier-return episode or lacked distinct anchors and consequences.
